headers.comment: The SPA shell must never be cached. Hosting matches a header rule against the REQUEST path, NOT the file the rewrite resolves to — so '/index.html' alone only covered a literal request for that path, and every real entry point ('/', '/plans', '/quotes' …) fell through to Hosting's default max-age=3600. Effect: for up to an hour after a deploy a returning admin kept the OLD HTML, which references the previous hashed bundle, so a shipped fix simply did not arrive. Verified live 19 Sep 2026: '/index.html' returned no-cache while '/' returned max-age=3600. The '!(*.*)' glob matches extensionless paths only, i.e. SPA routes — it cannot swallow /assets/**, whose filenames all contain a dot and which must stay immutable.

HTML and CSS are revalidated on every request. style.css has no content hash in its name, so any positive max-age means an edit (e.g. filling in a placeholder) stays invisible until the cache expires — which already cost one debugging round. These files are a few KB; caching them buys nothing.
Fonts are immutable — their names never change and their bytes never change.
